title: Understanding Mean Cubed Error
text: The Mean Cubed Error is calculated as the average of the cubed differences between the actual and predicted values. This means that the error is raised to the power of $$3$$.

title: Effect of Cubing the Error
text: Cubing the error means that larger errors will have a disproportionately larger impact on the loss compared to smaller errors. This is because cubing a number increases its magnitude significantly if the number is greater than $$1$$.

title: Comparing Mean Squared Error and Mean Cubed Error
text: Unlike Mean Squared Error, which penalizes errors quadratically, Mean Cubed Error penalizes errors cubically. This means that the penalty for larger errors is even more severe in Mean Cubed Error.

hintAnswer: Cubing amplifies both positive and negative errors leading to a larger overall loss for larger errors.
title: Analyzing the Impact of Cubing
text: Consider the impact of cubing on both positive and negative errors. How does this affect the overall loss?

hintAnswer: The model will be more sensitive to larger errors potentially leading to overfitting if not managed properly.
